examples.label: Exploit CVE-2014-3704 to create a new admin account

notes: Drupal 7 < 7.32 SQLi (CVE-2014-3704). It creates an admin account rather than direct RCE, so follow up by logging in and planting a webshell.
name: Drupalgeddon - Create Admin (CVE-2014-3704)
description: Exploits the Drupalgeddon SQL injection (Drupal 7 < 7.32) to create a new administrator account, giving full CMS control.

defense.why_it_works: Drupalgeddon (SA-CORE-2014-005 / CVE-2014-3704) exploits SQL injection in Drupal's database abstraction layer. Array-format username parameters bypass query sanitization, allowing insertion of a new admin user without authentication.
defense.prerequisites: Drupal 7.x before 7.32. Unauthenticated access to the registration or login endpoint.
defense.impact: Creates a new admin-level user, providing full backend access for further exploitation (webshell, data exfiltration).
defense.detection: Unusual POST parameters with array notation to Drupal's login endpoint. New admin user in the database. drupalgeddon.py request pattern.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (POST with array parameters) | Database: new user in users table with admin role | Drupal watchdog log (new user registration)
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*w3wp.exe" OR ParentImage="*httpd*" OR ParentImage="*apache*" OR ParentImage="*php-cgi*" OR ParentImage="*php-fpm*" OR ParentImage="*java.exe" OR ParentImage="*tomcat*")
| where match(Image, "(?i)(cmd|powershell|bash|sh|nc|python)")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine

index=web sourcetype=access_combined (method=POST OR status=500)
| stats count by clientip, uri_path | where count>3
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.parent.name:(w3wp.exe OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm OR java.exe) AND process.name:(cmd.exe OR powershell.exe OR bash OR sh OR nc OR python*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd","apache2","php-fpm","php-cgi","java.exe","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","bash","sh","nc","python")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
// Drupalgeddon (CVE-2014-3704) SQLi-to-RCE - apache/php spawning a shell
defense.prevention: Update to Drupal 7.32+. This vulnerability is over 10 years old -- any unpatched Drupal 7 instance should be considered fully compromised.
defense.misconfiguration: Drupal 7.x < 7.32 running on a public-facing server without the SA-CORE-2014-005 patch applied.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Drupal 7.x < 7.32
# Vulnerable query in includes/database/database.inc
# No parameterised query for array-type form values
defense.secure_config:
# Update to Drupal 7.32+ or Drupal 9.x
drush pm-update drupal
defense.evasion: Rename/obfuscate the uploaded webshell and delete it after use; prefer the app's built-in functionality (PHP filter / module) over dropping files; pace requests to blend with normal traffic.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Sysmon, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Creates a Drupal admin account via the Drupalgeddon SQLi (CVE-2014-3704):
  python2.7 drupalgeddon.py   the exploit
  -t http://<url>             target
  -u <newuser> -p <newpass>   the admin account it inserts
Drupal 7 < 7.32 mishandles the SQL API, letting the exploit inject a new administrator - giving full CMS control with no prior credentials.
